answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A garden delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A copper check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A haven penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 5956 identities need 5956 bonds of 30 tokens, 41734 dollars of hardware and 15 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
